trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down-left, down-right or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-left.

Going right would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up-left.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
The line must go up-right: down-right is number 20, which comes later.
Going up-right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
The line must go up-left: up-right is number 7, which comes later; right is number 8, which comes later.
Going down-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 7. So the line goes down-left.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-right.
Going down-right would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-right.
Number 9 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-right would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going right would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 19 before its turn. So the line goes down-right.

Going left would force the line onto number 19 before its turn; going down-left would strand number 14: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-3,3). So the line goes down-left.
Going up-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-left.
The line must go left: up-left is number 18, which comes later.
Going up-left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-3,3). So the line goes left.
Going up-left would cut off the bottom-left corner (3 cells); going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-right.
Going up-left would cut off the bottom-left corner (4 cells); going left would cut off the bottom-left corner (3 cells). So the line goes up-right.

Going up-left would leave both number 19 and cell (-1,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up-right would leave both number 19 and cell (1,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both (and 2 more options fail too). So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going left would turn number 19 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Cell (-3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 48 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 26 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 34/37 cells (92%).
Generation 1: fitness 26/37. The best line covers 36 cells, the first 26 of them still look solvable.
Generation 2: fitness 37/37. The best line covers 37 cells.
Generation 2: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 96 futures: 79% survive going down-left (best covers 70%); right 8%; down-right 4%.
Jackpot! A future after going up-left covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 37 cells x 37 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 3,162 variables and 8,576 clauses in 0.01 s (851 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.01 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
